ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Acute symptoms during maintenance therapy

A 31-year-old man receiving omalizumab for allergic asthma develops sudden wheezing and dyspnea after a viral respiratory infection. He asks whether an extra omalizumab injection will rapidly relieve the episode. Which explanation is most appropriate?

  1. An extra dose replaces the need to assess attack severity
  2. Maintenance treatment rules out a severe exacerbation
  3. The episode proves the patient has no allergic component to asthma
  4. Omalizumab is maintenance therapy and does not provide rapid rescue bronchodilation
  5. Omalizumab directly relaxes bronchial smooth muscle within minutes
Answer and explanation

Omalizumab is maintenance therapy and does not provide rapid rescue bronchodilation

The acute episode requires an appropriate reliever and severity assessment; an extra biologic dose is not rescue treatment.

Option explanations

Omalizumab is maintenance therapy and does not provide rapid rescue bronchodilation: The acute episode requires an appropriate reliever and severity assessment; an extra biologic dose is not rescue treatment.

Omalizumab directly relaxes bronchial smooth muscle within minutes: It modifies IgE-mediated inflammation rather than acting as a rapid bronchodilator.

An extra dose replaces the need to assess attack severity: Clinical severity still determines urgent treatment.

Maintenance treatment rules out a severe exacerbation: Exacerbations can occur despite biologic therapy.

The episode proves the patient has no allergic component to asthma: Breakthrough symptoms do not exclude allergic disease.
